title: Latin-script names — ICAO Doc 9303 §6.A folding with digraph options (Ä→AE, Å→AA, Ö→OE, Ü→UE)
description: Same as latin_icao but with ICAO's two-letter options for umlauts and ring: Ä→AE, Å→AA, Ö→OE, Ü→UE (Ñ stays N). This is the German-speaking and Nordic convention (Müller → MUELLER, Gößmann → GOESSMANN).
notes: ICAO §6.A rows: Ä 'AE or A', Å 'AA or A', Ö 'OE or O', Ü 'UE or UXX or U', Ñ 'N or NXX'. The first option is taken for Ä/Å/Ö/Ü; Ñ keeps N (NXX, App. B §B.4.1, is not produced).

Which issuers use the digraph options is not documented by ICAO; German, Austrian, Swiss and Nordic practice is the usual reference. Slovak ä, Turkish/Azerbaijani ö/ü and Estonian ä/ö/ü are normally folded to one letter (latin_icao).
All other letters, aliases and the ASCII fallback are inherited from latin_icao.
